# Public-Claim Repair Proposals, 2026-10-06

**Internal, generated, not deployed.** Generated by `node tools/claim-provenance/scan.mjs --write` from `tools/claim-provenance/lib/repairs.js` and a scan of the working tree.

**Status: implemented on the draft PR #39 branch on 2026-10-06, under the owner's repair authorization. Not published.** The repaired pages become public only if the owner separately approves a merge and publication. No repair changed a figure, a denominator or a date: each adds a missing qualifier, corrects a scope or label, or points a reader to the supersession notice. Every implemented repair is now a regression check: `scan.mjs --check` fails if a repaired page brings back the old wording or loses the applied wording.

Text is shown as visible text with markup removed. The surrounding markup and `data-panel` bindings were kept.

## PR-01 · `research.html` · CL-001 · IMPLEMENTED

**Was:**
> The detection panel, 16 independent reviewers across 11 countries and 5 continents, detected unreconstructable records at 83.9% accuracy against a verified key, clearing the threshold set before any data were examined.

**Now:**
> The detection panel, 16 independent reviewers across 11 countries and 5 continents, detected unreconstructable records in a constructed 24-record corpus at 83.9% accuracy against a verified key, clearing the threshold set before any data were examined.

**Reason:** Adds the constructed-corpus qualifier the register requires beside the detection figure (governing rule: constructed-record findings are not real-world performance).

## PR-02 · `research.html` · CL-004 · IMPLEMENTED

**Was:**
> A separate human-reviewer reliability analysis measured Gwet's AC1 at 0.739 for invited participants and 0.623 for open enrolment on 10 analysed records.

**Now:**
> A separate human-reviewer reliability analysis measured Gwet's AC1 at 0.739 for invited participants and 0.623 for open enrolment on 10 analysed records; the pre-registered two-part criterion was not met because neither lower confidence bound reached 0.41.

**Reason:** Adds the failed-criterion limitation the register records with the AC1 figures; elsewhere on the page it is stated, but not beside this sentence.

## PR-04 · `research.html` · CL-006 · IMPLEMENTED

## PR-05 · `research.html` · CL-011 · IMPLEMENTED

**Was:**
> Section 5.4 of the detection study reports that all five carry information separating a reconstructable record from an unreconstructable one, at p between 1.0e-08 and 1.5e-11 on 108 labels from 21 raters.

**Now:**
> Because the overall determination is built from the five conditions, their association with it is expected by construction; the detection study reports it descriptively (Appendix B) and makes no discrimination claim from it.

**Reason:** The 2026-08-29 detection manuscript moved this analysis to Appendix B with the inferential language removed as circular; the sweep records the derivation as deterministic; the employment manuscript makes no discrimination claim. The p-values are not evidence that the conditions discriminate, and "Section 5.4" no longer locates the analysis.

## PR-06 · `research.html` · CL-001 · IMPLEMENTED

**Was:**
> Panel detection 83.9% against a verified key ( 16 independent reviewers on the detection panel, 11 countries); cross-vendor raw agreement ranged 66.7 to 93.3 percent, mean 85.3 percent, across 61 recorded mixed-denominator runs, and 82.2 to 93.3 percent across 37 runs restricted to the full 15-record set, study closed 21 August 2026; no chance-corrected AC1 was computed for that cross-vendor study, so its pre-registered reproducibility criterion is not established; reviewer reliability Gwet's AC1 0.739 invited / 0.623 open enrolment, interim; the pre-registered two-part reliability criterion was not met because neither lower confidence bound reached 0.41.

**Now:**
> Panel detection 83.9% against a verified key on a constructed 24-record corpus (16 independent reviewers on the detection panel, 11 countries); cross-vendor raw agreement ranged 66.7 to 93.3 percent, mean 85.3 percent, across 61 recorded mixed-denominator runs, and 82.2 to 93.3 percent across 37 runs restricted to the full 15-record set as the series stood on 13 August 2026, study closed 21 August 2026; no chance-corrected AC1 was computed for that cross-vendor study, so its pre-registered reproducibility criterion is not established; reviewer reliability Gwet's AC1 0.739 invited / 0.623 open enrolment on 10 analysed records, interim; the pre-registered two-part reliability criterion was not met because neither lower confidence bound reached 0.41.

**Reason:** Adds three qualifiers the register requires: the constructed corpus, the 37-run window date and the 10-record reliability sample. No figure changes.

## Public downloads the scanner cannot read

The scanner reads visible page text and route string literals. It does not read PDFs. The deployed PDFs were inspected once by text extraction in this package session; one carries superseded claims. Each finding is bound to the file's sha256, so a changed file reopens it.

### PD-01 · `JRS_Reliability_Accuracy.pdf` · CL-033 · IMPLEMENTED 2026-10-06

- **Served as (before the repair):** research.html "Methods Paper · Reliability and Accuracy of JRS (Rungs 1 & 2)", through /api/dl?e=accuracy (api/dl.js: accuracy -> JRS_Reliability_Accuracy.pdf)
- **sha256 (unchanged):** `64bb9f80dd9f914210a7eb52ebf6a3f42cd16faa0b885aa22140d7995632b2b8`
- **Method:** One-off pdftotext extraction during the package session; not part of the deterministic scan.
- **Found:**
  - "Independent reviewers reached substantial agreement (Gwet's AC1 = 0.74 for experts, 0.63 for trained reviewers, across 10 records)."
  - "Cross-vendor AI agreement averaged 84% across 15 constructed records."
  - "The findings support reproducible application and substantial inter-rater reliability"
- **Reason:** A public download reports a superseded reliability characterisation and a reproducibility conclusion the current evidence does not support.
- **Proposal:** Do not edit the draft's text silently. Either replace the download with a version carrying the 29 August 2026 manuscript results, or add a first-page notice, exactly: "Superseded, 6 October 2026. This draft describes AC1 of 0.74 and 0.63 as substantial agreement and cross-vendor agreement as averaging 84 percent. The 29 August 2026 manuscript reports that the pre-registered two-part reliability criterion was not met and no longer uses the verbal band; the cross-vendor series closed on 21 August 2026 across 61 recorded runs (raw agreement 66.7 to 93.3 percent, mean 85.3 percent), and its reproducibility criterion is not established because the required AC1 was not computed. This draft is kept as a historical record."
- **Implemented:** The PDF is unchanged. A public notice page (methods-paper-notice.html) identifies it as an earlier draft, lists what the current record superseded or clarified, and links to the archived PDF through the existing download route. research.html and research-summary.html now link to the notice instead of the PDF. Notice: `methods-paper-notice.html`. Archival path: `/api/dl?e=accuracy&src=notice`.

| `methods-paper-notice.html`:111 | HISTORICAL | The draft reports that cross-vendor agreement averaged 84% across 15 constructed records, a figure from an earlier point in a nightly series. | Reports a withdrawn characterisation as history. |
| `methods-paper-notice.html`:113 | HISTORICAL | The draft says its findings support reproducible application and substantial inter-rater reliability. | Reports a withdrawn characterisation as history. |
| `research-summary.html`:205 | HISTORICAL | Earlier versions of this work placed 0.739 in the substantial band of Landis and Koch. | Reports a withdrawn characterisation as history. |
